AAPL.rationale: Apple's fundamental health is genuinely strong: Q2 FY2026 delivered +16.6% YoY revenue growth, +21.8% EPS growth, gross margin expansion of ~220 bps to 49.3%, and operating cash flow up 19.8% YoY. The balance sheet has improved dramatically with D/E falling from 1.42 to 0.78 in one year. Services revenue hit a record $30.98B at ~77% gross margins, and the 2.35B active device installed base with 92% retention rates underpins durable competitive advantage. However, the market has already priced this trajectory aggressively: at 37.5x trailing PE, the 2.7% earnings yield sits 175 bps below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.45%, leaving no margin of safety. The stock is at $312.51, within pennies of its 365-day high of $313.26, having rallied ~60% off its low. Valuation is mid-range vs own history (30.3x–43.1x) but absolute terms are stretched given the rate environment. Near-term catalysts are mixed: Q3 guidance of 14–17% revenue growth and the $100B buyback are supportive, but the three-front regulatory battle (Supreme Court App Store ruling, EU DMA, DOJ antitrust) could compress Services margins by $2–4B annually, and the CEO transition to Ternus introduces execution uncertainty. Oil at $92.65 is an unpriced hardware margin risk. The fundamental trajectory is healthy but the valuation fully reflects it, leaving a mildly positive but not compelling risk-reward.
